hook.text: Thomas Newcomen built the first practical steam engine in 1712—designed to pump water out of flooded coal mines.

buildup.text: Newcomen's engine was inefficient—wasting most of its energy heating and cooling the cylinder every stroke.

discovery.text: James Watt added a separate condenser in 1769—tripling efficiency and making steam power viable for factories.

twist.text: Watt's engine freed industry from rivers—factories could now be built anywhere coal could be delivered.

climax.text: By 1800, hundreds of Watt engines powered factories, mills, and mines—steam became the heartbeat of industry.

punchline.text: Steam freed industry from geography—build anywhere, power everything.
